skill.name: gh-issue-fix-flow
skill.description: Guide AI agents through GitHub issue intake, code changes, XcodeBuildMCP validation, commits, and pushes using gh and git.
skill.summary: Resolve GitHub issues through a structured fix, test, commit, and push workflow.
skill.author: Dimillian

security_audit.summary: All ten static findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code backticks in SKILL.md, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. The skill does guide agents to run gh, rg, XcodeBuildMCP, and git commands for user-authorized repository work. No prompt injection, hidden exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

remediation.issue: Remote push action lacks an explicit confirmation step.
remediation.suggestion: Add a step that asks the user to confirm before committing or pushing changes to a remote repository.

static_findings.snippet: 1. Use `gh issue view <id> --repo <owner/repo> --comments` to get the full issue context.
2. If the repo is unclear, run `gh repo view --json nameWithOwner` to confirm.
1. Use `rg -n` to locate likely files and entry points.
2. Read the relevant code paths with `sed -n` or `rg -n` context.
1. Check for unrelated changes with `git status --short`.

content.user_title: Fix GitHub Issues With a Guided Flow
content.value_statement: GitHub issue fixes can lose context across triage, edits, tests, and release steps. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code a repeatable workflow for issue resolution.
actual_capabilities: Retrieves GitHub issue details and comments with gh.
Guides code-path discovery with rg and focused file reads.
Directs minimal local edits that match repository style.
Uses XcodeBuildMCP for build and test validation.
Checks git status before staging selected fix files.
Creates a closing commit message and pushes the branch.
limitations: Requires gh authentication and repository access.
Requires user authorization for local edits, commits, and pushes.
Best suited to projects that use XcodeBuildMCP validation.
Does not replace maintainer review or CI policy.

use_cases.title: Resolve App Bugs
use_cases.description: Take a reported GitHub issue from context gathering through tested code changes and a closing commit.

use_cases.title: Contribute Focused Fixes
use_cases.description: Follow a disciplined path for reproducing an issue, editing the right files, and reporting validation results.

use_cases.title: Standardize Fix Workflows
use_cases.description: Give coding agents a consistent process for issue intake, testing, commit hygiene, and final reporting.

prompt_templates.title: Fix One Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-issue-fix-flow to fix issue 123 in this repository. Inspect the issue, make the smallest correct change, test it, and report results.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a Specific Repository Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-issue-fix-flow for issue 123 in owner/repo. Confirm the repository, read comments, implement the fix, run validation, and summarize changes.

prompt_templates.title: Fix With Targeted Tests
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-issue-fix-flow to resolve issue 123. Add or update focused tests when practical, run XcodeBuildMCP validation, and include failures if any remain.

prompt_templates.title: Complete and Push a Fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gh-issue-fix-flow to resolve issue 123 in owner/repo. Keep changes minimal, run builds and tests, commit with a closing message, and push.

output_examples.input: Fix issue 118 about a failing macOS build.
output_examples.output: Inspected issue 118, corrected the build setting, ran the macOS build, committed the fix, and pushed the branch.

output_examples.input: Resolve issue 42 and include test results.
output_examples.output: Updated the affected code path, added a focused test, ran simulator validation, and reported one unrelated warning.
Read the issue comments, identified the likely module, found missing reproduction detail, and reported the blocker before editing.

best_practices: Confirm the repository, branch, and issue number before editing.
Keep changes small and cite validation results in the final report.
Review git status before staging to avoid unrelated files.
anti_patterns: Pushing changes when the issue scope or repository is unclear.
Hiding failing tests or warnings in the final report.
Staging unrelated files with the intended fix.

faq.question: What does this skill automate?
faq.answer: It structures a GitHub issue fix from issue review through code changes, validation, commit, push, and final reporting.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub access?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow expects gh authentication and repository permissions for reading issues and pushing changes.

faq.question: Can it work without XcodeBuildMCP?
faq.answer: It is designed around XcodeBuildMCP. Other build tools need separate repository instructions.

faq.question: Will it edit code automatically?
faq.answer: It guides an agent to edit code after issue review. Users should confirm scope and permissions first.

faq.question: Does it handle unrelated local changes?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to check git status and stage only files related to the fix.

faq.question: Is it suitable for production repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, when used by authorized maintainers with normal review, CI, and branch protection policies.
